backlog.spec: Give _solve_once an optional argument gamma (default 0). The SLSQP objective becomes -(sum(r) + gamma * sum(r**2)). In the basin-hopping loop, call it with gamma = rng.uniform(-2, 2) on half of the steps and gamma = 0 on the others. Positive gamma favours unequal radii, negative gamma favours equal radii, so the solver is pushed towards different size distributions and contact graphs. Candidates are still scored and accepted by the plain repaired sum of radii. When a candidate from a step with gamma != 0 comes within 0.002 of the incumbent sum, run one more _solve_once from it with gamma = 0 before the acceptance test, so that it is compared at a true local optimum.
backlog.title: Convex radius bonus in the hop objective

backlog.spec: At each basin-hopping step generate 3 perturbed starts (each with the smallest-circle relocation), run SLSQP with maxiter=25 on each, and fully continue (maxiter 200) only the one with the highest partial radius sum after repair-free evaluation (sum of radii minus total overlap violation). Accept as before.
backlog.title: Multi-candidate relocation with real solves screening

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, with probability 0.3 per step, replace the perturbed radii r0 with 0.7 * br (the incumbent radii scaled down uniformly) instead of br plus Gaussian noise. Centres still get the usual N(0, 0.02) noise and the _relocate call. This gives SLSQP room to rearrange the contacts before the circles regrow. All other steps (the usual radius noise) stay unchanged.
backlog.title: Radius-reset kick

backlog.spec: Add a parameter maxiter to _solve_once (default MAX_ITER). In the basin-hopping loop use maxiter=80 for each candidate solve. If the repaired candidate sum is within 0.002 of the incumbent or better, re-run _solve_once from the candidate's centres and radii with maxiter=400, repair, and compare that result with the incumbent instead. This gives more hops per second while still converging the promising ones fully.
backlog.title: Cheap hops with a full re-solve only on improvement

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, draw sigma = exp(rng.uniform(log(0.005), log(0.05))) once per step and use it for both the centre noise and the radius noise in place of the fixed 0.02. Steps then mix fine local refinements with larger escapes, with no schedule to tune. Everything else stays the same.
backlog.title: Log-uniform random perturbation size per step

backlog.spec: Keep a pool of the 5 best distinct packings (distinct by sum differing by >1e-5). With probability 0.2 per step, build a child by choosing a random vertical or horizontal line at coordinate u~U(0.3,0.7), taking circles from the best packing on one side and from a different pool member on the other side, then fixing the count to n by dropping the smallest overlaps or adding relocated smallest circles. Solve with SLSQP from this child, repair, and insert into the pool.
backlog.title: Elite pool crossover

backlog.spec: In _solve_once add 'ftol': 1e-10 to the SLSQP options dict (keep maxiter=MAX_ITER). SciPy's default ftol of 1e-6 can stop the solve before contacts are fully tight, and the repair step then loses some radius. This is a one-line change with no other edits.
backlog.title: Tighter SLSQP ftol in every basin-hopping solve

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop of solve, replace the radius perturbation r0 = max(br + N(0, 0.02), 0) with a deterministic deflation r0 = 0.85 * br (new constant DEFLATE = 0.85). Keep the centre noise of sd 0.02 and the _relocate call as they are. The aim is that SLSQP starts from a nearly feasible point with slack around every circle, so it can rearrange and regrow, instead of starting from random overlaps of about 0.02 that force large first steps. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Deflated feasible start for each hop

backlog.spec: Use MAX_ITER=60 for basin-hopping solves (warm-started from a perturbed incumbent, they usually converge quickly) and keep 200 for the first solve. Gives more hops per 24 s. Optionally if the 60-iteration result has a sum within 0.01 of the incumbent, re-run it with the remaining 140 iterations warm-started from the result.
backlog.title: Adaptive SLSQP iteration cap

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, call _relocate twice in a row with probability 0.5 (using rng), and once otherwise. After the first call the moved circle usually has a larger radius, so the second call moves the next smallest circle. This allows moves that need two small circles shifted at once, which single relocation followed by greedy acceptance cannot reach. Add the constant DOUBLE_PROB = 0.5. _relocate itself, the noise and the acceptance rule do not change.
backlog.title: Relocate the two smallest circles per hop

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, change the pair non-overlap constraint from sqrt(dist^2) - r_i - r_j >= 0 to the smooth form dist^2 - (r_i + r_j)^2 >= 0, where dist^2 = ((c_i - c_j)**2).sum(1). This removes the sqrt, whose gradient is badly behaved when centres nearly coincide after the relocation and noise step, and gives SLSQP's finite differences a polynomial constraint. Leave the wall and r >= 0 constraints as they are. Leave _repair unchanged, since it still checks true distances and keeps the packing valid. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Squared-distance pair constraints

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, after adding noise, clip each centre to [r0_i, 1 - r0_i] (using the perturbed, non-negative radius, capped at 0.5) instead of to [0, 1]. Do the same in _relocate, which already picks feasible radii. This gives SLSQP starting points that never violate a wall constraint. Apply the clip after the radius noise is computed and before _relocate. No other change.
backlog.title: Clip perturbed centres to stay inside the walls

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random initial centres in the first _solve_once by a Halton sequence in bases 2 and 3 with a random Cranley-Patterson shift (add rng.uniform(size=2) mod 1), scaled to [0.05,0.95]. Keep INIT_RADIUS. Only the first start is affected.
backlog.title: Halton start with random scramble

backlog.spec: After the basin-hopping loop ends (at TIME_FRACTION of the budget), run one more SLSQP solve starting from the best (centres, radii). Use options={'maxiter': 1000, 'ftol': 1e-12} through a new optional parameter of _solve_once (default stays as now). Clip the centres to [0,1], repair, and keep the result only if its repaired sum of radii beats the incumbent. Check the clock inside the polish: if less than 3 s remains before time_limit, skip it. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Final tight-tolerance SLSQP polish of the incumbent

backlog.spec: In _relocate, pick the circle to move at random with probability proportional to 1 / (r_i + 0.01)^2, using the seeded rng, instead of always argmin(r). The same small circle then is not moved every step, and other near-rattlers also get tried. The trials and the scoring stay unchanged.
backlog.title: Inverse-radius-weighted relocation target

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, alternate between two kinds of kick on successive steps. On even steps perturb only the centres (radii copied from the incumbent). On odd steps perturb only the radii (centres copied from the incumbent, with noise sd 0.02 applied to radii only). Keep _relocate and the acceptance rule unchanged. The goal is to separate topology moves from size moves so each is less likely to be undone by the other.
backlog.title: Alternating perturbation axis

backlog.spec: After the basin-hopping loop ends at TIME_FRACTION of the time, run one extra SLSQP solve from the unperturbed incumbent (x0 = concatenate([bc.ravel(), br])) with options maxiter=300 and ftol=1e-12. To do this, give _solve_once optional maxiter and ftol arguments and pass them into the options dict; the in-loop calls keep the defaults. Clip the centres, apply _repair, and replace the incumbent only if the repaired sum is larger. Before starting, check that at least 4 s of CPU time remain (time.process_time() - t0 < time_limit - 4); skip the polish otherwise. The aim is to recover the roughly 1e-6 to 1e-4 slack left by the default ftol and the proportional shrinking in _repair.
backlog.title: Final tight-tolerance SLSQP polish of the incumbent

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, remove the four wall blocks (c-r, 1-c-r) and the r>=0 block from cons and instead pass bounds to minimize: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]. Keep only the pair-distance constraints in cons plus wall constraints c-r>=0 and 1-c-r>=0 (these are still needed, so keep them), but drop the redundant r>=0 block by using bounds on r. This shrinks the constraint vector and speeds each SLSQP solve, allowing more basin-hopping steps in the time budget.
backlog.title: Native box bounds for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Extend _relocate with a parameter force (default False). When force is True, after the best point p is chosen, set the moved circle's radius to the median of r instead of the hole radius rk, capped by the distance from p to the nearest wall. Then, for every other circle j that now overlaps it, set r[j] = max(d_j - r[k], 0.2 * r[j]), where d_j is the centre distance. The small circle is thus planted as a full-size circle and its neighbours give way. Plain relocation leaves it as a small circle in a hole, and SLSQP then tends to push it straight back. In the loop, call _relocate with force=True with probability 0.3 (constant FORCE_PROB), chosen with rng. SLSQP, _repair and greedy acceptance are unchanged.
backlog.title: Forced-size insertion with neighbour deflation

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 0.02 noise sd in basin hopping with an adaptive sigma starting at 0.02. After each step multiply sigma by 1.2 if the candidate improved the incumbent, otherwise by 1.2**(-0.25). Clip sigma to [0.003, 0.08]. Use sigma for both centre and radius noise.
backlog.title: One-fifth-rule perturbation sigma

memo: Helped: basin hopping replacing random restarts (slot 1, -2.9313/-2.9274) and relocating the smallest circle before each solve (slot 23, -2.9353/-2.9339; incumbent -2.9346 over 2 runs). Gains are close to the noise sd of 0.0034, so be cautious. Single unconfirmed runs 0.0019 or more better than the incumbent: slot 25 two-cluster merge start (-2.9366), slot 26 weighted objective (-2.9365), slot 30 two-stage wall tightening (-2.9368), slot 31 hard-disk Monte Carlo start (-2.9364). Did not help: longer time fraction (-2.9204), tied-radii start (-2.9225), penalty continuation (-2.9048), subset re-optimisation (-2.8822), symmetric start (-2.9155), pair-list pruning (-1.7220, broke the packing). Init changes, extra moves and heavy restructuring mostly failed or were neutral. Next: replicate slots 25, 26, 30 and 31, then stack the best one or two on the relocation move. Also try small in-loop tweaks such as swapping a small and a large circle. Keep edits small. The gap to the published 2.9370 is about 0.003.
